title: WPSB/397/2014 of STATE OF UTTARAKHAND Vs MADAN GOPAL PUSHKARANA

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/B) No.397 of 2014
State of Uttarakhand and another .......Petitioners
Vs.
Madan Gopal Pushkarana .........Respondent
Present :
Shri B.P.S. Mer, learned brief holder for the
State/petitioners.
Shri M.C. Pant, learned counsel for the respondent.
22nd December, 2020
Coram : Hon'ble Ravi Malimath, A.C.J.
 Hon'ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
Alok Kumar Verma, J. (Oral)
This writ petition is filed seeking a writ of certiorari
to set aside the judgment and order dated 06.01.2014
passed by the Public Services Tribunal, Uttarakhand at
Dehradun (hereinafter referred to as, "Tribunal") in Claim
Petition No.32 of 2011, "Madan Gopal Pushkarana vs. State
of Uttarakhand and another" whereby learned Tribunal has
allowed the claim petition preferred by the respondent and
the impugned order dated 11.04.2008, awarding censure
entry as well as the order passed in departmental appeal are
quashed.

2
2. In order to appreciate the issues involved in this
writ petition, the relevant facts need mentioned infra.
3. The facts, to the limited extent necessary, are that
while working as Superintending Engineer, P.W.D. Circle 24,
Dehradun, a charge-sheet dated 11.04.2007 was served
upon the respondent by the Enquiry Officer, Additional
Secretary, Public Works Department, on the allegations that
the respondent had acted negligently and in violation of
Finance Rules in issuing the orders for the supply of Road
Signage. The respondent submitted his reply dated
19.04.2007 and had explained that he had acted in
conformity with the established practice and procedure of
the department and in accordance with Finance Rules.
Subsequently, the enquiry report dated 11.06.2007 was sent
by the Enquiry Officer to the State Government, which was
considered along with the representation dated 18.08.2007
of the respondent and he was found having committed the
mischief. Therefore, the respondent was awarded censure
entry vide order dated 11.04.2008. Against the said order
dated 11.04.2008, the respondent submitted his
representation dated 16.04.2008 for expunging the censure
entry. The representation of the respondent was rejected on
15.10.2008. Aggrieved, the respondent challenged both the
orders i.e. 11.04.2008 and 15.10.2008 in his claim petition
before the Tribunal.
4. After hearing both the parties, the Tribunal
allowed the claim petition. The impugned order of the
censure as well as the order passed on departmental appeal
are quashed by the Tribunal.

3
5. The Tribunal referred to a judgment of Punjab and
Haryana High Court in Ram Kumar Goel vs. State of
Haryana, 1991(5) SLR 263, cited by the respondent herein,
in which it has been laid down that once the procedure is
initiated for inflicting the major penalty then that procedure
had to be followed irrespective of the fact that only a minor
penalty has been imposed.
6. Learned Tribunal observed once the procedure for
an enquiry is adopted that should be followed by the
disciplinary authority. The procedure should not be broken
on the ground that only the minor punishment is to be
awarded. In the present case it is admitted that the
proceedings of enquiry was initiated which is prescribed for
inflicting major penalty, which has not been followed and
this fact goes against the respondents consequently the
enquiry proceedings cannot be held justified. Apart from the
above fact, it is also important that copy of the enquiry
report was not supplied to the petitioner. The above two
facts vitiate the proceedings of enquiry. Learned Tribunal
further observed that in the present case, the
representation/departmental appeal has been disposed off
by the same authority, whereas the appeal or representation
should have been decided by an officer who is higher in rank
to that of disciplinary authority.
7. Learned counsel for the State submitted that for
the illegality committed by the respondent, an enquiry was
conducted against him in terms of the Uttarakhand
Government Servant (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2003
(hereinafter referred to as, "the Rules, 2003"). The
respondent was charged with one misconduct and the same

4
was found to be proved and accordingly censure entry, a
minor penalty, was imposed on the respondent. The
observation of the Tribunal that once the charge was framed
against the respondent, it was mandatory for the petitioners
herein to conduct the enquiry as prescribed for inflicting the
major penalty as has been provided under Rule 7 of the
Rules, 2003, cannot be sustained since only minor penalty
has been imposed not major penalty. The respondent cannot
ask for adopting the procedure which is prescribed for
awarding major penalty.
8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the
respondent submitted that the Enquiry Officer has not
conducted any enquiry against the respondent. The Enquiry
Officer neither informed him the place, date and time of the
enquiry nor supplied any enquiry report/findings of the
Enquiry and the petitioner no.1 herein has issued the
impugned order dated 11.04.2008 without following the
rules. No opportunity was given to him for hearing.
Therefore, there is no illegality in the impugned judgment
and order, passed by the Tribunal.
9. We have heard rival contentions of the learned
counsel for the parties through video conferencing.
10. The respondent is a Government Servant and his
service so far as disciplinary matters are concerned, is
governed by the Rules, 2003. Rule 3 thereof deals with the
minor penalties and major penalties. The four penalties viz.,
(i) Censure; (ii) Withholding of increments for a specified
period; (iii) Recovery from pay of the whole or part of any
pecuniary loss caused to Government by negligence or

5
breach of orders; (iv) Fine in case of persons holding Group
"D" posts are classified as minor penalties and four penalties
viz., (i) Withholding of increments with cumulative effect;
(ii) Reduction to a lower post or grade or time scale or to a
lower stage in a time scale; (iii) Removal from the Service
which does not disqualify from future employment; (iv)
Dismissal from the Service, which disqualifies from future
employment are classified as major penalties.
11. Rule 7 of Rules, 2003 contains the procedure for
imposing major penalties. Sub-rule (vii) of Rule 7 runs thus,
"Where the charged Government Servant denies
the charges the Enquiry Officer shall proceed to call
the witnesses proposed in the charge-sheet and
record their oral evidence in presence of the charged
Government Servant who shall be given opportunity
to cross-examine such witnesses. After recording the
aforesaid evidences, the Enquiry Officer shall call
and record the oral evidence which the charged
Government Servant desired in his written
statement to be produced in his defence;
Provided that the Enquiry Officer may for reasons
to be recorded in writing refuse to call a witness."
12. Rule 9 of Rules, 2003 provides for action on
enquiry report. According to sub-rule (4) of Rule 9 if the
Disciplinary Authority, having regard to its findings on all or
any of charges, is of the opinion that any penalty specified in
Rule 3 should be imposed on the charged Government
Servant, he shall give a copy of the enquiry report and his
findings recorded under sub-rule (2) to the charged
Government Servant and require him to submit his
representation if he so desires, within a reasonable specified
time. The disciplinary authority shall, having regard to all
the relevant records relating to the enquiry and

6
representation of the charged Government Servant, if any,
and subject to the provisions of Rule 16 of these rules (Rule
16 stipulates consultation with the Commission), pass a
reasoned order imposing one or more penalties mentioned in
Rule 3 of these rules and communicate the same to the
charged Government Servant.
13. Rule 10 of Rules, 2003 provides for procedure for
imposing minor penalties. Rule 10 runs thus:-
"10.(i) Where the Disciplinary Authority is satisfied
that good and sufficient reasons exist for adopting
such a course, it may, subject to the provisions of
sub-rule (2) impose one or more of the minor
penalties mentioned in Rule 3.
(ii) The Government Servant shall be informed of
the substance of the imputations against him and
called upon to submit his explanation within a
reasonable time. The Disciplinary Authority shall,
after considering the said explanation, if any, and
the relevant records, pass such orders as he
considers proper and where a penalty is imposed,
reason thereof shall be given, the order shall be
communicated to the concerned Government
Servant."
14. An analysis of above mentioned provisions would
clearly show that summary procedure is to be followed for
imposing minor penalty. For major penalty an enquiry is a
condition precedent. If the charged Government Servant
wants to lead his evidence in support of his plea, it is
essential that he should be given an opportunity to lead such
evidence. The failure on the part of the enquiry officer to fix
a date for recording such evidence and give due intimation
to the charged Government Servant is a clear violation of
statutory requirements. As regards minor penalties, the
rules prescribe that no such penalty shall be imposed unless

7
the Government Servant is informed in writing the
substance of the imputations against him, he is given an
opportunity to submit his explanation and that explanation is
considered by the Disciplinary Authority. Having regard to
the mandatory provision of the rules regulating imposition of
minor penalties, no minor penalty can be imposed unless the
prescribed procedure is followed.
15. When the disciplinary authority initiates
proceedings under the rules which prescribe the procedure
for imposing a major penalty, it is obligatory for the
disciplinary authority to hold the enquiry in conformity with
the rules. The mere fact that ultimately a minor penalty is
imposed cannot be taken as the basis for an argument that
any defect in holding the enquiry stands cured. The non-compliance with the mandatory provision in holding the
enquiry vitiates the final order, though it imposes only a
minor penalty and though the disciplinary authority could
have imposed the said penalty without following the
procedure prescribed for a major penalty. Once the enquiry
proceedings are vitiated for violation of the rules under
which the enquiry is held, such an enquiry proceeding
cannot be taken as the basis for imposing any penalty.
16. Thus, in view of the above, the penalty order is
not maintainable in the eye of the law.
17. In view of the above detailed discussion, we are of
the considered view that learned Public Services Tribunal
has not erred in law or on facts. We do not find any
perversity or infirmity in the impugned judgment and order

8
warranting interference. Therefore, the writ petition is liable
to be dismissed.
18. In the result, the writ petition is dismissed. No
costs.
(Alok Kumar Verma, J.) (Ravi Malimath)
 A.C.J.
